extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and feature coverage of wartime events and the role of war correspondents, as presented in a newspaper front‑page/dispatch format. Includes official statements about correspondent mission, casualty reports, and examples of frontline reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide frank and complete information about the war
rubrics_metrics.description: Bravery of American correspondents and enterprise of the American newspapers... have given the American people frank and complete information about the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated by the Office of War Information (Elmer Davis) as a mission-level standard: reporting should aim to give the public a frank, complete account of wartime events. The page supports this with examples of accredited correspondents in many theaters and their dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mirror for home what fighting men are doing
rubrics_metrics.description: “Their mission is to mirror for us at home something of what our fighting men are doing for us. Whatever they may tell about themselves is but incidental to giving us the best understanding they can of those with whom they are joined.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correspondents should focus on conveying the experience and actions of combat forces rather than self-promotion. The page cites OWI text and gives context (numerous correspondents active in front-line theaters) as exemplars of this principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bravery and acceptance of risk (non-combatant courage)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The gallantry of these reporters and photographers is akin to that of our fighting men... For they don't fight—and they can't fight back when, as it happens so often, their own lives are jeopardized.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are expected to accept personal danger to report the war; page documents accreditation numbers (600+ accredited, ~400 active), casualties (15 have died, many wounded or missing), and specific examples (Webb Miller, Ralph Barnes, Leo Disher, etc.) to illustrate the standard and its consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed with forces / accompany units to accurately reproduce situations
rubrics_metrics.description: “Only by accompanying our air fighters did they feel they could reproduce the war situations descriptively for the radio and reading public.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate descriptive reporting often requires being physically present with military units (air, naval, ground). The article lists many theaters and instances where correspondents accompanied operations to produce firsthand accounts.
